findings.title: pass_open's displayed signature omits its real full_state keyword
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:299 — "pass_open(cfg, round; regrade = false, sweep_ok = false, io = stdout) -> Int"
src/CLI/Passes.jl:324-325 — "function pass_open(cfg::AbstractDict, round::AbstractString; regrade::Bool = false, sweep_ok::Bool = false, full_state::Bool = false, io::IO = stdout)"
findings.description: The docstring's own displayed signature line for pass_open lists only regrade, sweep_ok and io, but the method defined two lines later also takes full_state::Bool = false — which the docstring's own arguments bullets two lines further down DO document. The argument is documented in prose but missing from the signature header shown to the reader.
findings.resolution_hint: Add full_state = false to the displayed signature line at Passes.jl:299.

findings.title: makedocs docstring claims every non-zero check errors, but the closure gate's non-zero return is swallowed as a skip
locations: src/DocLints.jl:17-19 — "Any non-zero return is an `error`, so the build fails."
ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:32-38 — frozen-round skip returns nothing on a non-zero gate code
findings.description: The makedocs docstring's own next paragraph says the wrapper returns nothing when an open round of a docs instrument froze the build, so the blanket claim two sentences earlier — 'Any non-zero return is an error' — is false in exactly the default frozen-round case, unless GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP is set.
findings.resolution_hint: Qualify the sentence to carve out the frozen-round skip described in the following paragraph.

findings.title: demote()'s rendered docstring cites a bare section number, which RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS forbids
locations: src/CLI/Demote.jl:18 — "§12 records the fork, content against emptiness"
findings.description: RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS forbids a rendered docstring citing a section number or inaccessible source. demote()'s rendered prose (inside the triple-quoted docstring, not a # comment) cites '§12' plus an unlinked historical round id and finding id, none resolvable from a REPL read of ?demote. This is exactly the pattern SCAN.DEAD_REF's own regex is built to catch.
findings.resolution_hint: Move the historical justification to docs/design-record/ or ARCHITECTURE.md; keep the docstring self-contained.

findings.title: gbg selftest --pinned's docstring claims it runs the QUICK doctor, but the code runs a bespoke narrower selection
locations: src/CLI/Selftest.jl:10-11 — "runs the QUICK doctor there — the pinned-copy behaviours (PIN.SELF, PIN.TREESHA, PIN.SOURCES)"
findings.description: The QUICK doctor is a specific named preset in Doctor.jl that does not even include PIN.SELF or PIN.TREESHA, and does include many checks the actual --only "PIN,CFG.VALID,SELF.CONSUMER" call never runs. Calling this bespoke selection 'the QUICK doctor' misdescribes what actually executes.
findings.resolution_hint: Replace 'runs the QUICK doctor there' with a description of the actual --only selection.

findings.title: release()'s closing condition for the cited rc round is narrower than what cites_round actually accepts
locations: src/CLI/Release.jl:43-44 — "closed by honored or adjudicated ids"
src/CLI/Release.jl:24-26 — accepts closed_by in (honored, adjudicated, rescan, seeded) or a carried id
findings.description: release()'s docstring (matching CLAUDE.md's Release checklist verbatim) states the precondition as ids closed by honored or adjudicated ids, but cites_round actually accepts a materially wider set including rescan, seeded closures, or carried ids.
findings.resolution_hint: Align the docstring (and CLAUDE.md) with the real accepted set, or tighten cites_round to match the documented rule.

findings.title: SCAN.XLINK's suggested manual fix uses a different link form than Reflection.xlink's own auto-apply
findings.description: The dry-run hit suggests a two-part qualified link with an implicit target, but Reflection.xlink(apply=true) — the function the scan itself calls — writes a bare-name link text with an explicit three-part target for the identical case. The manual guidance and the automatic fix disagree.
findings.resolution_hint: Make the Hit's suggested text match what apply=true actually writes.

findings.title: formula_in_backticks.jl's comment misstates its own regex's real false positives
locations: src/Scans/formula_in_backticks.jl:1-3 — pattern shown includes ≠ but the false-positive list names ×, ⋅, ≈
findings.description: The comment displays FORMULA_GLYPHS as [≤≥≠∈∉∇Δ⟨⟩‖√×⋅], then names its false-positive class as ×, ⋅, ≈ — but ≈ never appears in the pattern at all, while ≠, which is in the pattern and is a real Julia operator (used legitimately elsewhere in this package, e.g. `frozen ≠ ideal` in TestHarness.jl), is omitted from the exemption list.
findings.resolution_hint: Correct the comment to name ×, ⋅ and ≠ as the real-operator false positives; drop ≈.
findings.contradicts: the pattern literal shown one line earlier in the same comment

findings.title: Fleet.rows' MISSING status is never named in either docstring's enumeration
locations: src/CLI/Fleet.jl:7-10 — enumerates only OK, NOT-INITIALISED, BEHIND, RED
src/CLI/Fleet.jl:70 — code assigns status = "MISSING" for a nonexistent path
findings.description: Both the Fleet module docstring and the Fleet.rows function docstring enumerate exactly four status values, and the function docstring even separately states 'a missing path is exit 2' without naming the status string. The code produces a fifth, distinct status literal, MISSING, that appears in neither enumeration.

findings.title: apply_ledger's docstring overstates when a scan-scope wildcard entry fully disables a scan
locations: src/Scan.jl:344-346 — describes scan-scope target="*" as always disabling
src/Scan.jl:357 — code requires target=="*" && !haskey(e,"match") to disable a scan-scope entry
findings.description: For scope=policy, target * alone disables, matching the docstring. For scope=scan the code additionally requires the entry to carry no match table; one that does falls through to per-hit matching instead. The docstring's combined sentence omits this exception for the scan-scope case.
findings.resolution_hint: Split the sentence to state the match-table exception for scan-scope wildcard entries.

findings.title: cmd_install's docstring overstates that success always means two files were written
locations: src/CLI/Install.jl:36-38 — "Returns 0 when both files are written"
findings.description: The docstring's own preceding sentence says the dev pointer file is written only with --dev-checkout. Without that flag only one file (the shim) is ever written, yet the function still returns 0 on success, so 'both files' overstates the ordinary flag-less success path.
findings.resolution_hint: Reword to 'Returns 0 on success (the shim always, the dev pointer only with --dev-checkout)'.
